subject: Problem set release: timeline, submission instructions, and reviewer allocation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@gmail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Problem set — backend/frontend engineer (prompt + timeline)

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for taking the time to interview with us. As discussed, attached is the candidate problem set for the backend/frontend engineer role. This is an asynchronous exercise intended to show design thinking and implementation approach — you can pick either a full-stack mini-feature or a focused backend design + API implementation.

High-level details:
- Attachment: backend_frontend_takehome_prompt_v2.pdf (PDF) — includes spec, required deliverables, and optional stretch goals.
- Deadline: complete submission by Mon, Feb 22, 2027 at 11:59 PM PT (we allow a single 48-hour extension with prior notice).
- Format: Github repo (private), a short README with run instructions, and a 6–10 minute recording showing the app or design walkthrough.
- Submission: send link to kimberly@redwood.ai and cc aditya_rao@redwood.ai. If you want to keep the repo private, add kimberly@redwood.ai as a collaborator or provide an archive.

We’ll confirm reviewers once submissions come in. Expected turnaround for feedback is 3 business days after submission. Attached is the grading rubric we’ll use to score the assignment.

Attachments: [attachment: backend_frontend_takehome_prompt_v2.pdf (PDF, 2.1 MB)], [attachment: grading_rubric_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB)]

If anything is unclear or the deadline is tight, let me know and we can discuss a short extension.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Recruiting Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@gmail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Problem set — backend/frontend engineer (prompt + timeline)

Hi Kimberly — thanks for sending this over and for the clear instructions. Quick questions: 1) For the recording, is a screencast with voice-over acceptable or do you prefer a webcam + screen share combo? 2) Are we required to use a specific stack (I generally use Node/Express + Postgres)?

Also, I may be traveling on the 20th–21st; could I request the 48-hour extension up front (so new deadline Mon 24th)? No problem if you want to hold to the original date.

Thanks,
Sam
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Problem set — backend/frontend engineer (candidate questions & extension request)

Folks — forwarding Sam's questions. He asked about the recording format and asked proactively for the 48-hour extension because of travel on Feb 20–21.

Can Marcus or Lauren confirm reviewer assignment for this role and whether we can grant the extension if needed? Ideally we want 2 reviewers from Eng (one backend, one frontend) + hiring manager. Marcus, can you: 1) confirm who will cover backend review and 2) if we should share the rubric link and any reviewer notes in advance? Lauren, if you can own the frontend reviewer that would be great.

Context: candidate is solid from interviews so far; this is to validate system design + implementation. We prefer the extension to be explicit — if granted, update candidate with new deadline Mon, Feb 24 11:59 PM PT.

Thanks — Kim

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Problem set — backend/frontend engineer (candidate questions & extension request)

Kim/Kevin/Team — I can cover backend review and coordinate with Eric Cho (not on this thread) for deeper performance checks if needed. Lauren — thanks for taking frontend.

Quick answers to Sam's questions (please confirm before I send to candidate):
- Recording: screencast with voice-over is fine. No requirement for webcam.
- Stack: any reasonable stack is acceptable; we care about architecture, testing, and clarity. Node/Express + Postgres is fine.
- Extension: OK to grant the 48-hour extension given travel, new deadline Mon, Feb 24 11:59 PM PT.

I'll prepare reviewer checklist and share rubric link (drive folder) with reviewers. We should request the repo link and the short recording in the submission email. I can take lead on scoring backend criteria on the attached rubric; Lauren to score frontend and UX.

Attachments: [attachment: reviewer_checklist.md (MD, 2 KB)]

—Marcus
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@gmail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Problem set — backend/frontend engineer (prompt + timeline)

Hi Sam — quick follow-up to confirm: we’re happy to grant the 48-hour extension. New submission deadline: Mon, Feb 24, 2027 at 11:59 PM PT.

Recording: a screencast with voice-over is perfect. Stack: use whichever stack you prefer (your Node/Express + Postgres stack is fine).

When you submit, please: 1) share a private GitHub link or archive, 2) include a README with run instructions and notes on decisions, and 3) attach or link to the 6–10 minute walkthrough recording. We’ll notify reviewers (Marcus + Lauren + hiring manager) and aim to return feedback within 3 business days.

Attachments: [grading_rubric_v1.xlsx] (see drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-kim-takehome)

If you want help with delivery options while traveling, ping me and we can work around timezones. Good luck — looking forward to seeing this.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Recruiting Manager
Redwood Inference
